hook: She beat every man by 15 hours, and it's not even the craziest part.
story: The Spine Race runs the length of England's Pennine Way in January: 268 miles of snow, bog and darkness, and the clock never stops. In 2019, Jasmin Paris entered - a veterinary lecturer with a baby daughter at home. The record for the whole race, set by a man, was over 95 hours. Paris finished in 83 - twelve hours faster than anyone had ever run it. And at the checkpoints, while her rivals slept, she stopped to pump milk for her baby.
number: Second place arrived 15 hours after her. Her closest challenger never arrived at all: he was pulled off the course, hypothermic, four miles from the finish.
full_text: She beat every man by 15 hours, and it's not even the craziest part. The Spine Race runs the length of England's Pennine Way in January: 268 miles of snow, bog and darkness, and the clock never stops. In 2019, Jasmin Paris entered - a veterinary lecturer with a baby daughter at home. The record for the whole race, set by a man, was over 95 hours. Paris finished in 83 - twelve hours faster than anyone had ever run it. And at the checkpoints, while her rivals slept, she stopped to pump milk for her baby. Second place arrived 15 hours after her. Her closest challenger never arrived at all: he was pulled off the course, hypothermic, four miles from the finish. Can your mom do it?
